papers.title: Reframing Parkinson's disease as an aging phenotype: Insights from stage-stratified integrative medicine and cerebrovascular-metabolic comorbidity.
Interest in clinical trial participation in Parkinson's disease: Insights from a nationwide registry.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare (socio-)demographic, clinical, and functional characteristics of Parkinson's disease (PD) patients interested in clinical trial participation with those who are not. BACKGROUND: Representative recruitment is essential for clinical trials. Identifying factors associated with interest in participation may help tailor trial designs and recruitment strategies. METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from a nationwide PD registry in Austria. Participants were dichotomized according to interest in clinical trial participation at inclusion, and group differences were statistically determined. Predictors of interest were selected using logistic regression with LASSO regularization. RESULTS: Among 543 PD patients, 395 (72.7%) expressed interest in clinical trial participation. Interested patients were younger (67.65 ± 10.16 vs. 72.76 ± 9.08 years, p < 0.001), had a shorter disease duration (9.24 ± 6.81 vs. 11.68 ± 8.64 years, p = 0.003), and less advanced disease, reflected by lower Hoehn and Yahr-stages (median 2.00 ± 1.00 vs. 3.00 ± 1.00, p < 0.001) and MDS-UPDRS-scores (all p < 0.001). Interested patients were also less likely to be functionally dependent (36.2% vs. 58.5%, p < 0.001), receive care allowance (24.8% vs. 41.9%, p < 0.001), or live in care facilities (2.8% vs. 10.1%, p = 0.001). Sex and motor fluctuations did not differ (all p > 0.085). LASSO regression identified absence of postural instability and dementia, younger age, and not being widowed as the strongest predictors of positive interest to participate in clinical trials. papers.title: Subjective cognitive decline as an early marker of cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment is one of the non-motor symptoms with the greatest impact on patients and caregiver quality of life. Given its onset and significant relevance during the prodromal phase of Parkinson's disease (PD), and its potential role as an at-risk state for cognitive impairment, this study investigated the role of subjective cognitive decline in PD (PD-SCD) as an early prognostic marker of subsequent cognitive impairment to enhance timely detection and prediction. Additionally, it evaluated how mood-related symptoms (depression, anxiety and apathy) influence this relationship. Data from 577 people with Parkinson's disease (PwPD) and 308 control participants from the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) cohort, together with 142 PwPD from the Luxembourg Parkinson's Study cohort, were analyzed over four visits. PD-SCD, with a baseline prevalence of 21.66% in PPMI and 18.31% in the Luxembourg Parkinson's Study, was associated with an at-risk state for cognitive decline over time. Higher levels of mood-related symptoms (apathy, depression, and anxiety) were observed in the PD-SCD group compared with the people with Parkinson's disease presenting normal cognition group (PD-NC) depending on the cohort. In addition, apathy and depression were cross-sectionally associated with higher levels of subjective cognitive complaints (SCC), underscoring their role as a key feature of the PD-SCD clinical profile, without masking the association between PD-SCD and cognitive impairment. Overall, PD-SCD emerged as a relevant at-risk state of cognitive impairment in PD and as a potential dynamic tracker of cognitive impairment trajectories, highlighting its clinical relevance within the continuum of cognitive impairment in PD.

papers.title: Clinical utility of MANAGE-PD: a cross-sectional study to characterize Parkinson's disease patients in Türkiye.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: MANAGE-PD is a clinical decision-support web-based tool that facilitates healthcare professionals in determining patients with Parkinson's disease who are inadequately controlled on oral medications. This was the first national, non-interventional study aimed to assess the distribution of patients throughout MANAGE-PD categories, and the clinical characteristics, concordance with physician assessment and tool categorization, and usability of the tool MANAGE-PD in Türkiye. METHODS: Patients were classified into three treatment groups based on symptom control and therapeutic requirements: adequately controlled on current oral therapy (Category 1), inadequately controlled with a recommendation for oral therapy optimization (Category 2) and inadequately controlled with a recommendation for both oral optimization and consideration of device-aided treatment (DAT) (Category 3). The main outcome was the proportion of patients in the MANAGE-PD categories. Secondary outcomes included clinical features within each group, agreement between MANAGE-PD categorization and physician assessment, planned therapy changes, physician-rated acceptability, and completion time. Clinical evaluations included MDS-UPDRS, NMSS for motor and non-motor symptoms, as well as the PDQ-8 for quality of life. The ease of use of the MANAGE-PD tool was assessed by the physicians using Visual Analog Scale. RESULTS: A total of 514 PD patients from 16 sites were included in the study, of whom 217 patients (42.2%) were adequately controlled on current oral treatment (Category 1), 122 patients (23.7%) were classified as having potential for oral therapy optimization (Category 2), and 175 patients (34.0%) were not well controlled and might benefit from DAT (Category 3). The MDS-UPDRS and NMSS scores exhibited an increase from Category 1 to Category 3, indicating an elevated burden of both motor and non-motor symptoms. PDQ-8 scores demonstrated a reduction in quality of life across categories.

papers.title: From intestinal barrier sensing to glial immune programming: a barrier-immune-glia relay in microbiota-associated neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota contributes to host homeostasis through metabolic, immunological, neural, and barrier-related pathways, and its role in the onset and progression of neurodegenerative diseases has received increasing attention. Patients with Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis often exhibit alterations in gut microbial composition, microbial metabolic function, and peripheral inflammatory phenotypes. However, existing clinical evidence is derived predominantly from cross-sectional studies, and the direction of causality between microbiota alterations and disease pathology remains to be established. This review uses a "barrier-immune-glial relay" framework to systematically summarize the potential mechanisms through which gut microbiota-associated signals influence immune homeostasis in the central nervous system. First, alterations in microbial composition, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, tryptophan derivatives, and lipopolysaccharide may act on the intestinal epithelial barrier, enteric nervous system, and intestinal mucosal immune cells, thereby affecting local immune tolerance and inflammatory responses. Second, intestinal macrophages, dendritic cells, innate lymphoid cells, T cells, and B cells may translate local microbial signals into circulating metabolites, inflammatory mediators, and immune cell-associated signals, which may in turn influence blood-brain barrier function and the central immune microenvironment. Furthermore, microglia and astrocytes, as key integrators within the central nervous system, can respond to gut-derived metabolites and peripheral immune signals. Their interaction network may determine whether neuroinflammation, synaptic injury, and neurodegenerative pathology are amplified or constrained. This review also evaluates the levels of evidence supporting these mechanisms in Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and multiple sclerosis. papers.title: Mitochondrial protein import stress augments α-synuclein aggregation and neural damage.
papers.abstract: Genetic and environmental factors are known to converge on mitochondria to cause Parkinson's disease. The underlying mechanism is incompletely understood. In addition to bioenergetic defects, nonbioenergetic pathways have been largely unexplored. papers.title: Mouse APOE Christchurch protects against Aβ-induced tau and α-synuclein aggregation.
papers.abstract: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype alters the risk for Alzheimer's disease (AD) but also affects dementia risk in Parkinson's disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). Recent evidence suggests that the APOE Christchurch (CC) mutation protects against AD, however, its effects on PD and DLB are unknown. We generated an APOE CC knock-in mouse to understand its effects on amyloid-β (Aβ), tau, and α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregation. APOE CC mice show increased plasma cholesterol and triglyceride levels, decreased Aβ and Aβ-induced tau pathology after intracortical AD-tau injection into 5xFAD mice but do not change Aβ or tau pathology in individual transgenic mouse models without injection. Interestingly, APOE CC reduces formation and spread of α-syn aggregation in the brain, peripheral-to-spinal cord spread, and directly increases binding affinity to α-syn compared to APOE WT. Our study emphasizes the remarkable protective effects of a point mutation in murine APOE against Aβ-induced tau and α-syn aggregation.

papers.title: KBN2201 attenuates the hippocampal astrocytic NOX4-MPO/OPN axis and restores mitochondrial protein markers not recovered by chronic L-DOPA in an MPTP mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: The basis of the hippocampal, non-motor pathology of Parkinson's disease (PD) remains incompletely defined. We previously described an astrocytic axis in the PD hippocampus in which myeloperoxidase (MPO) and osteopontin (OPN) are induced in parallel downstream of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4). Here, in male C57BL/6J mice given a chronic (28-day daily) MPTP regimen, we asked whether oral KBN2201 (OPTBA), a hybrid ester of 2-hydroxy-4-trifluoromethyl benzoic acid and pyruvate, is associated with attenuation of this axis. L-DOPA served as a dopaminergic comparator, co-administered throughout the MPTP regimen. The reported behavioral outcomes were obtained seven days after the final dose, before tissue collection. KBN2201 (5 and 20 mg/kg) improved rotarod and grip-strength performance, preserved nigrostriatal tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons, and reduced α-synuclein immunoreactivity in the dentate gyrus and the substantia nigra, with a significant reduction in the striatum at 20 mg/kg. In the dentate gyrus, MPTP increased astrocytic NOX4, MPO, and OPN. Hippocampal immunoblotting showed increased levels of 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE)-modified protein adducts and reduced levels of the mitochondrial protein-import components TIM23 and TOM20 together with oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) complex subunits I-V. KBN2201 attenuated each change and restored Ki67- and doublecortin (DCX)-positive cell populations. L-DOPA also improved motor performance, reduced 4-HNE-modified protein adducts, MPO, OPN, and α-synuclein in the dentate gyrus, and restored Ki67-positive cells, but did not restore NOX4 protein, TIM23, TOM20, or any OXPHOS subunit, whereas both KBN2201 doses did. Motor improvement can therefore occur without recovery of the hippocampal mitochondrial protein marker profile.

papers.title: Familial ATP10B R303W variant links autophagy-lysosome dysfunction to α-synuclein accumulation in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: ATP10B gene was implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD) through lysosomal dysfunction, however, its direct association with α-synuclein (α-syn) pathology remained unclear. Here, a potential pathogenic ATP10B R303W variant was identified from 45-year-old Korean man and investigated in a familial case of early-onset PD. Genetic analyses confirmed a familial heterozygous ATP10B R303W mutation in PD within the family. Structural modeling predicted the destabilized local interactions, which altered physicochemical properties. To characterize the functional impact of the variant, ATP10B R303W (heterozygous) and SNCA A53T (positive control, homozygous) cells were generated using CRISPR/Cas9. Cells were evaluated for their mitochondrial functions, oxidative stress, autophagy, lysosomal activity, and α-syn accumulations. ATP10B R303W cells exhibited the reduced mitochondrial membrane potentials and the elevated reactive oxidative oxygen species in comparison to wild type (WT). The decreased LC3-II/I ratio indicated the impaired autophagosome formation in ATP10B R303W cells. Compromised Lysosomal function was confirmed by the increased pH, reduced membrane permeability, decreased β-glucocerebrosidase activity, and diminished Lysotracker staining. Live-cell imaging of pHrodo-labeled α-syn revealed the increased fluorescence progressively in ATP10B R303W cells. Significantly, the accumulated α-syn was noticed in the cytosolic and membrane fractions of ATP10B R303W cells, where the reduced α-syn levels were found in the supernatant. Phosphorylated α-syn displayed an increasing trend, exceeding the levels in SNCA A53T cells. Our findings provided additional evidence from a previous study on lysosomal impairment of ATP10B variants by demonstrating the first evidence of promoted pathological α-syn accumulations by ATP10B R303W. papers.title: Distinct sympathoneural and cardiovagal domains of arterial baroreflex function in autonomic synucleinopathies.
papers.journal: Clinical autonomic research : official journal of the Clinical Autonomic Research Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The arterial baroreflex has sympathoneural and cardiovagal efferent limbs. Whether quantitative measures represent interchangeable indicators of a single physiological construct has been unclear. Moreover, the extent to which results agree in the synucleinopathies pure autonomic failure (PAF), Parkinson disease with or without orthostatic hypotension (PD + OH, PD No OH), and multiple system atrophy (MSA) remains incompletely understood. In a retrospective observational study we comprehensively assessed physiological and neurochemical biomarkers of arterial baroreflex function in these disorders. METHODS: Data for 10 baroreflex-sympathoneural and 6 baroreflex-cardiovagal indices were compared among 38 patients with PAF, 63 with PD + OH, 63 with PD No OH, and 72 with MSA, along with a pooled Control group (130 total; 44 with complete autonomic baroreflex datasets). RESULTS: Indices of baroreflex-sympathoneural and baroreflex-cardiovagal function were only weakly correlated. Within the two domains, correlations across subjects were much stronger. Among sympathoneural measures, pressure recovery time after the Valsalva maneuver, the logarithm of the total baroreflex area, and the fractional orthostatic increment in plasma norepinephrine best distinguished patients with autonomic synucleinopathies from controls. Among cardiovagal measures, the Baroslope derived from Phase II of the Valsalva maneuver and the logarithms of low- and high-frequency heart rate variability during supine rest were the most informative. No baroreflex measure separated PAF from PD + OH or MSA. CONCLUSIONS: Indices derived from blood pressure and interbeat interval responses during the Valsalva maneuver capture much of the physiologically meaningful variation in baroreflex function and enable efficient assessment of the sympathoneural and cardiovagal limbs in autonomic synucleinopathies.

papers.title: Neuronal AIMP2-α-synuclein synergy drives endogenous tau and amyloid-β pathologies and neurodegeneration in a mechanistic model of Lewy body dementia.
papers.abstract: Lewy body dementia (LBD), encompassing Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), is defined by widespread α-synuclein (αSyn) aggregation and frequently exhibits coexistent tau and amyloid-β (Aβ) pathologies. However, whether αSyn pathology is sufficient to drive endogenous tau and Aβ aggregation has remained unclear due to a lack of in vivo models that recapitulate the full spectrum of LBD-associated proteinopathies and neurodegeneration. AIMP2, a parkin substrate that accumulates in Parkinson's disease, enhances αSyn aggregation and toxicity, but its role in initiating downstream mixed pathologies across vulnerable brain regions has not been demonstrated in vivo. Here, we generated a conditional, neuron-specific Tet-Off double-transgenic mouse model enabling post-developmental coexpression of AIMP2 and A53T αSyn. This synergistic coexpression induced rapid and widespread αSyn aggregation, detergent-insoluble Lewy-like inclusions, mitochondrial degeneration, synaptic impairment, and neuronal loss, accompanied by marked gliosis. Mice developed key clinical features of LBD, including progressive cognitive impairment, bradykinesia, and olfactory deficits. Notably, without tau or APP overexpression, endogenous tau became hyperphosphorylated through dysregulated kinase signaling, and Aβ accumulated predominantly as TBS-soluble Aβ42 monomers/oligomers without fibrillar plaque deposition, demonstrating that AIMP2-αSyn-driven pathology is sufficient to trigger downstream tauopathy and Aβ pathologies. These mixed pathologies were associated with lysosomal and proteasomal dysfunction, evidenced by p62 and polyubiquitinated protein accumulation. Proteomic analysis identified dysregulation of pathways linked to amyloid processing, synaptic trafficking, and protein quality control. papers.title: Ferroptosis as a Therapeutic Target in Neurological Disorders: Pharmacological Advances and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-mediated form of programmed cell death characterised by distinct features, including excessive iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and impaired antioxidant mechanisms. The susceptibility of the Central Nervous System (CNS) to ferroptosis has been reported, along with evidence that ferroptosis is associated with neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), stroke, and Multiple Sclerosis (MS). To date, major ferroptosis inhibitors encompass iron chelators, lipid-trapping antioxidants, and antioxidant modulators. Translational challenges in drug toxicity, selectivity, and delivery promote drug development in terms of improving pharmacokinetics through structural modification, alternative routes of administration, and nanoparticle encapsulation. In addition, research on identifying novel and promising ferroptosis inhibitors from natural products and known drug compounds is continuous, accompanied by ongoing drug optimisation and modification. Biomarkers of ferroptosis have been discussed given the emerging clinical interest in them for disease diagnosis or prognosis and patient stratification. Standalone anti-ferroptotic treatments for CNS disorders have been found to be difficult to achieve favourable clinical outcomes, thereby suggesting combination therapies that not only harness ferroptosis but also address diverse pathological pathways in the respective diseases as a prospect for managing CNS disorders. Thus, this article aims to review recent updates on clinically approved ferroptosis inhibitors as well as summarise the current drug development landscape and outline future directions to provide a better understanding of the contemporary development of ferroptosis inhibitors for neurological disorders.

papers.title: Minimal Clinically Important Differences of Common Anxiety Scales in Older Adults with Parkinson's Disease with Anxiety Following Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To establish minimal clinically important difference (MCID) thresholds for the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Anxiety Subscale (HADS-A), Parkinson's Anxiety Scale (PAS), and Geriatric Anxiety Inventory (GAI) in older adults with Parkinson's disease and anxiety (PD-A), and identify optimal thresholds for classifying clinical improvement. METHODS: This cohort study included 110 older adults with PD-A who completed individualized Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT). Anxiety was assessed before and after intervention using the four scales. Clinical change was anchored to the Global Rating of Change (GRoC) scale. MCIDs were estimated using anchor- and distribution-based methods. RESULTS: Anchor-based between-group mean-change estimates yielded MCIDs of -2.38 (BAI), -3.64 (HADS-A), -3.13 (PAS), and -2.95 (GAI). Receiver operating characteristic analysis using the Youden index identified complementary classification cut-offs of ≤ -2 for the BAI, HADS-A, and PAS, and ≤ -1 for the GAI. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides MCID thresholds for four anxiety measures in older adults with PD-A, offering clinically relevant benchmarks for interpreting treatment-related changes and evaluating improvement. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Clinicians can use the estimated MCID thresholds to interpret whether changes in anxiety scores following CBT are likely to represent clinically meaningful improvement in older adults with PD-A. The complementary ROC-derived cutoffs may assist in identifying individual improvement, while combined use of anxiety measures, particularly the PAS and HADS-A, may enhance sensitivity to clinically meaningful change.

papers.title: Combining transcranial electrical and magnetic stimulation: a scoping review of neurophysiological and clinical studies.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Clinical response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) is variable. Combining these techniques may improve effectiveness. The aim of this review is to map how rTMS and tES have been combined so far in both neurophysiological and clinical studies. METHODS: Three databases were searched: Embase, MEDLINE, and APA PsychInfo. Included articles compared a combination of rTMS and tES, against a single form of stimulation (either rTMS or tES). RESULTS: Sixty-seven articles were included. Forty studies examined the impact of combined stimulation on a measure of neurophysiology in healthy volunteers. Most studies targeted the motor cortex (25) and used transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) (25) combined with a form of rTMS, either applying stimulation simultaneously (19) or with tES priming of rTMS (14). Twenty-seven studies used combined stimulation to treat people with a health condition (including people with tinnitus, depression, bipolar, Parkinson's disease, and post-stroke motor deficits). CONCLUSIONS: Studies indicate that tES could enhance or reverse expected effects of rTMS. The greatest increase in cortical excitability occurred following excitatory rTMS combined with gamma transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) or with cathodal tDCS, consistent with effects of metaplasticity. Cathodal tDCS combined with excitatory rTMS has shown promise for treating depression and post-stroke motor deficits. SIGNIFICANCE: This review highlights combined stimulation as a promising method to modulate and enhance the neurophysiological and clinical effects of rTMS and tES. Insights from neurophysiological studies may guide development of more effective clinical treatments.

papers.title: A Portrait of Anxiety and Depression in Parkinson's Disease: Prevalence, Clinical Correlates, and Treatment Gaps.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-motor symptoms (NMS), specifically anxiety and depression are major drivers of disability in Parkinson's disease (PD). Prevalence estimates remain inconsistent because of differences in population samples, diagnostic criteria, and symptom overlap, contributing to underdiagnosis and undertreatment. OBJECTIVES: This retrospective, cross-sectional study examined the prevalence, comorbidity, and clinical correlates of anxiety and depression using dimensional severity scales and multivariate modeling. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed de-identified records from 1221 patients assessed by a single neurologist specializing in PD patient care. Mood symptom severity was evaluated using Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) and Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) criteria. Logistic regression models identified associated factors for relevant anxiety (BAI ≥13) and depression (BDI ≥14). RESULTS: Clinically relevant anxiety (42%) and depression (30%) and anxiety-depression comorbidity (24%) were found to be consistent with previous estimates, with a high prevalence of mild depression (33%). Regression models identified sleep disturbance as a primary associated factor for both mood symptoms. Functional impairments involving hygiene, walking, swallowing, sensory complaints, and speech were associated with one or both mood symptoms. Left lower-extremity bradykinesia and right-sided tremor were associated with both mood symptoms. Significant "treatment" and "remission" gaps were also observed, as prescriptions for anxiolytics and antidepressants were significantly associated with relevant anxiety and depression. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight pervasive diagnostic and therapeutic gaps and the relationship between mood symptoms and functional disability. The limited efficacy of pharmacological monotherapy underscores the need for multi-dimensional tools and integrated treatment approaches to improve recognition and management of mood symptoms in PD.

papers.title: Adjunctive Multisensory Passive Immersive Virtual Reality With Synchronized Plantar Tactile Stimulation for Gait and Balance Disorders in Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Postural-locomotor disorders, particularly freezing of gait and postural instability, are among the most disabling symptoms of advanced Parkinson's disease (PD) and respond only partially to dopaminergic therapy. Evidence for virtual reality (VR) approaches in moderate to severe PD remains limited. This prospective randomized controlled open-label exploratory trial evaluated the addition of multisensory passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation to conventional rehabilitation for gait, balance, and freezing disorders in moderate-to-severe PD (Hoehn and Yahr Stages 2-4). In the study, 80 PD patients were randomized into an experimental group (EXP, n = 40) receiving standard pharmacotherapy and conventional rehabilitation plus 10 sessions of passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation and a comparison group (COM, n = 40) receiving standard pharmacotherapy and conventional rehabilitation only. Because the VR sessions were added to an otherwise identical program, the trial evaluates the effect of adding this intervention rather than a VR- or tactile-specific effect. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 10 days using the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and Freezing of Gait Questionnaire (FoG-Q). The EXP group showed significant improvements in the UPDRS "Gait" cluster (an eight-item composite of UPDRS items 2.11, 2.12, 2.13, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13, range 0-32; median from 12.5 to 8.0 points, p < 0.001), BBS (from 38.0 to 43.5 points, p < 0.001), and FoG-Q (from 9.0 to 6.5 points, p < 0.001). papers.title: Natural Glycosides in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Multi-Target Mechanisms via the Gut-Brain Axis.
papers.abstract: The multifactorial complexity of neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, limits the efficacy of single-target therapies. Natural glycosides exhibit promising neuroprotective potential, but their clinical translation is hindered by poor oral bioavailability and limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration. The gut-brain axis offers a framework for understanding their potential biological effects beyond direct central exposure. This review explores the multi-target mechanisms of natural glycosides in NDs, focusing on their interactions with the gut-brain axis. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect for studies published up to June 2026. Relevant literature on glycosides, NDs, gut microbiota, microbial biotransformation, pharmacokinetics, and neuroprotective mechanisms was critically reviewed. Natural glycosides may affect ND-related processes through gut-mediated and systemic/central mechanisms. Poorly absorbed glycosides can interact with intestinal microbiota, potentially modulating microbial composition, intestinal barrier integrity, and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) production. Microbial biotransformation may generate metabolites with altered physicochemical properties and systemic exposure, potentially enhancing central nervous system accessibility in a compound-specific manner. Experimental evidence also suggests effects on neuroinflammation, mitochondrial homeostasis, autophagy, and synaptic function. However, most findings remain preclinical, with limited direct human evidence. The gut-brain axis provides a valuable perspective for understanding the biological activities of natural glycosides despite their limited oral bioavailability and BBB penetration. Further pharmacokinetic studies, causal investigations of microbiota-mediated effects, and controlled clinical trials are needed to establish their therapeutic potential in NDs.

papers.title: Emerging strategies for progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) combination therapies.
papers.abstract: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterised by a combination of motor, ocular, cognitive, and behavioural impairment, but has a heterogeneous clinical presentation. It is a devastating and rapidly progressive atypical parkinsonian disorder with no current disease-modifying treatments. PSP is classified as a primary tauopathy characterised by abnormal accumulation of tau within neurons and glial cells, primarily in the brain stem, culminating in cell death. While genome wide association studies have been instrumental in identifying multiple risk loci, recent multi-omics studies combining brain gene expression and other omics measures have revealed a plethora of perturbed transcripts and molecular pathways that may play pivotal roles in PSP. This includes genes such as MAPT, STOM, KANK2, DDR2, LRRK2, and STX6, but their precise roles remain elusive. These genes are differentially expressed and may regulate processes including neuroinflammation, glymphatic clearance of tau, cytoskeletal maintenance, and synaptic function. In this review, we summarise current treatment strategies attempted in PSP, compile disease-modifying therapies in development, and explore potential disease mechanisms suggested by multi-omics studies. By targeting several underlying disease processes at once, combination strategies have the potential to improve both motor and cognitive function, slow neurodegeneration, and ultimately alter disease progression.
